title: His mother, brothers and sisters, and father Giles Moore
summary: Mother took in washing; Moore was the youngest of five children; he names his brothers and father and says no sibling played music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let's back up a bit, Fred, and talk about your mother and father and your grandparents. Your mother worked around the home. Were her parents living?
I think she had about one or two... Her uncle, his name was... Her last name was Cherry(?), but I was so
Moore (I) - 9

young to know what... My mother used to take in washing and ironing to keep us...to help raise us, you know. She did that kind of... There was two or three of us, myself and my brother Eddie. Of course, I was the youngest one. I was about, oh, three or four years older [sic] than my brother. That's the only one who's living, is my brother -- he's living in North Carolina. I guess he must be now around 85 years old.
And you are the youngest.
I'm the youngest.
So there were three boys altogether, and no girls...
Yes.
No sisters.
Myself and Johnny Moore and Eddie Moore, the three boys...,
Yes.
...and two sisters. There was five altogether.
Oh.
Oh yes, there's one more; I forgot to mention his name. A brother next to (?)...Will... His name was Wilmore. He was the oldest one.
Wilmore.
Wilmore. My brother Eddie was next to Wilmore.
Moore (I) - 10
I see. Were any of these siblings involved in music or entertainment? Or were you the only one?
No. I'm the onliest one.
I see. Did you know your father's people, his mother and father?
No, I didn't know none of those. All I know is... I just remember my mother used to tell me this was her husband. His name was Giles. Giles Moore.
Giles Moore.
I don't remember him, I was so young.
Yeah. You were essentially a babe in arms.
Yeah. They said I was around nine weeks old or something around there. Ten weeks old.
